speaker: Dash
intro: Dash Delgado: owner, chef AND only driver of Speedy Slice! Hot or it's free. Can we do this in twenty?
A pizza boss in a hurry! We'll be quick AND careful, Dash.
I woke up yesterday and my right ear was just... gone. Probably wax. Can you be quick?
Gone overnight? Hold on to your pizza. This could matter a lot.

always_clues.text: Right ear went overnight, yesterday morning

options: Exactly when did it start?
Yesterday, when I woke up. There was a pop, then whooshing. About thirty hours ago?
Pop, then whooshing: about 30 hours ago
onset
Thirty hours. Sooner is better, so let's keep moving!
What's the best pizza topping?
Pineapple. Fight me. Actually, don't, I'm busy.
Has your hearing ever done this before?
Never. The right was perfect until yesterday. I hear my scooter fine with the left.
First time ever: right ear fine until yesterday
first_time
Any pain, drainage, or dizziness?
No pain, no drips. A bit wobbly yesterday, fine now. Just the whoosh.
No pain or drainage
red_flag_check
Have you tried cleaning it out?
I tried a cotton bud. Nothing came out. Pretty sure it's wax though.
Tried a cotton bud: nothing came out
cotton_bud
Never poke in there! And 'probably wax' is a guess. We'll look.
Can I get a free pizza?
Only if it arrives cold. Mine never do. Which is why we must HURRY.

joke_line: Tasty, but not a clue. Ask about his ear!

red_flags.ask_line: Always ask about red flags: pain, drainage, dizziness.
red_flags.answer: No pain, no drips. A bit wobbly yesterday, fine now. Just the whoosh.
red_flags.card:
Sudden, one ear, yesterday: YES. Dizzy too.
See a doctor. How soon? You decide.

after_history: Any face droop, numbness, slurred speech or double vision? Those mean the ER now.
None of that. Just the ear.
A sudden loss in one ear, yesterday. Quick AND careful: let's look.

otoscopy.caption: Dash's RIGHT ear: an average-sized canal. No wax at all!
lines: Clear canal, healthy eardrum. Not a speck of wax!
No wax? Then what's blocking it?
Maybe nothing is blocking it. Let's check the middle ear next.

quiz.prompt: Dash says it's wax. Does the tymp agree?
options: No: a normal peak and a normal canal volume.
Yes: it's flat, like a wax plug.
A wax plug gives a flat line and a small canal volume. His peak is normal.
A tymp can't tell.
It can! A wax plug flattens the curve and shrinks the canal volume.

tymp.clue: Tymp: type A both ears (no fluid, no wax plug)
after: Type A both sides: no fluid, no wax plug. The bone test shows if it's deeper.

instructions: Tell him: press for every beep, even faint ones. No racing the beeps!
Beeps only. Fast but accurate. Like my deliveries!

audiometry.intro: Better ear first, like the pros. Left at Hoot speed!
Right ear's yours. Start at 1k, as always.
Bone check at Hoot speed: where is the trouble?
before: Wax would block air but not bone. The bone buzzer will tell us!

after_audiometry: Masked bone is in. Let's see where it landed.

reveal.title: ONE EAR, OVERNIGHT
ask: One ear down overnight. Now: where did the masked bone land?
lines: Right ear needs 40 to 60 dB, left ear normal. One ear, overnight.
Not wax, not fluid: bone is down too. That's what makes it urgent.
Sooner is better. Doctors still treat after three days, but today beats tomorrow.

evidence.prompt: What type of loss is Dash's right ear?
options: Sensorineural: bone is down with the air.
Conductive: blocked, like wax.
Mixed: a bit of both.
wrong: Then bone would be near normal. His masked bone is down with the air.
Mixed needs a gap too. His bone and air sit together.
evidence.right: Sensorineural and sudden: the inner ear or nerve changed overnight.

findings.text: Right ear down, bone too: inner ear or nerve

lines.today: Hot delivery! Sudden sensorineural loss is urgent: treatment works best early. Doctor TODAY!
lines.fit: Hold the pizza! A brand-new sudden loss needs a doctor first, and today.
lines.refer: A routine referral could take weeks. A sudden loss can't wait: TODAY.

clue_pick.prompt: Present the evidence: why TODAY and not next month?
clue_pick.wrong_line: True, but that wouldn't make it a rush. What makes it urgent?

wrong_lines.no_wax: No wax rules out a plug. What makes it a rush?
wrong_lines.tymp_a: That rules out fluid and wax. What makes it a rush?
wrong_lines.cotton_bud: Never poke in there! But that's not the rush. Look again.
wrong_lines.red_flag_check: No pain is good news. What makes it urgent?
wrong_lines.left_normal: That's his good ear. What happened to the other one?

right_lines.dizzy: Yes! Dizzy with a sudden loss: another red flag. Today.

clue_pick.right_line: Exactly! Sudden, one ear, inner ear or nerve: the doctor sees him today.

payoff: Hoot here, Booth Camp. Sudden loss in the right ear since yesterday. Can you see him today?
Three o'clock? Perfect. His audiogram is on its way to you now.
Dash, the ear doctor sees you at three. Go straight there, pizzas or not.
Same day? Faster than my pizzas! Thanks, owl!

headlines.S: SUDDEN LOSS SPOTTED IN RECORD TIME; PIZZA STILL HOT
headlines.A: PIZZA BOSS RUSHED TO EAR DOCTOR SAME DAY; TOPPINGS DEBATE CONTINUES
headlines.B: DASH SENT TO DOCTOR TODAY; OWL CHECKS WATCH
headlines.C: SOME BEEPS ARRIVED COLD, CONFIRMS OWL
headlines.Do-over: TRAINEE DEMANDS REMATCH; DASH ALREADY AT THE DOCTOR

subheads.S: One ear, overnight, bone down too: a same-day referral. Sooner was better.
subheads.A: A sudden one-sided loss can't wait: doctor today.
subheads.B: The call was right; a few stamps wandered.
subheads.C: Sudden plus sensorineural means doctor today.
subheads.Do-over: Remember: sudden hearing loss is urgent, even after three days. Dash made his appointment anyway.
